concept: Rotary is the knob of the appliance: a flat disc with one printed index mark over a ring of detent ticks across 270 degrees, dyed orange as the unit's one loud part, that turns with the hand and settles into the nearest detent on the material's spring.

default_to_avoid.pattern: skeuomorphic chrome audio plugin knob with gradients, knurling and a glowing LED arc
default_to_avoid.why_not: P6 allows no gradients and no glow outside the displays, and P3 says a rotary is a circle with one index mark, so the value is never told by a lit arc.

default_to_avoid.pattern: drag-only rotary knob with no keys, no printed value and no label
default_to_avoid.why_not: P3 gives every mechanism its keyboard map and a visible value and label, so a knob is a slider that arrows step and Home and End reach.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver and RT 20 radio (Dieter Rams, 1961–63): flat tuning knobs with a single index line over a printed scale
Braun H 1 / HZ heaters and the KF 20 era thermostats: one coloured control knob among body-coloured parts
apps/lab/anchor (D-001, card A): the orange tuning knob at 0.36 of the unit's short side with 11 detents over 270°

derivation.consequence: rotaries are circles with one index mark
derivation.form: The knob is a flat disc with corner.round and a single printed index line running inward from its rim, with no knurl, cap or arc.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: kind primary paints the disc action.accent with an action.accent-rim edge; kind key is a body-coloured disc for secondary dials.

derivation.consequence: the loud control is the one round or largest part
derivation.form: The default diameter follows corner.knob-ratio, 0.36 of the unit's short side, so the knob is the largest part of the unit.

derivation.consequence: rotaries and faders settle into the nearest detent
derivation.form: Dragging turns the disc directly; on release or a key press it settles into a detent on a spring of mass 1.4, stiffness 520 and damping 46.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map (arrows step a detent, Home and End reach the ends, Space and Enter press) and a visible value and label
derivation.form: The disc is a role slider: arrows step one detent, PageUp and PageDown several, Home and End the ends, and the value and label are printed below it.

derivation.consequence: no gradients, no glow except P2's emitters
derivation.form: The disc is one flat dyed colour with the shared part shadow; the tick ring is printed ink and nothing lights up as the value changes.

options.name: flat disc with one printed index line over a printed tick ring
dimple disc: a recessed finger dimple as the index, dot ticks
fixed pointer on the case, numerals on a turning plastic skirt with an orange cap

variants.reason: A is anchor card A's knob and P3's circle with one index mark, and its ink line stays legible at 44px and survives forced colours as a border; B's orange dimple loses contrast at small sizes, and C turns its numerals upside down and splits the orange into a cap on a skirt.

root.why: The knob, its printed value and its label stack in one column so the printing sits with the part it names.

dial.why: The dial area holds the disc and its tick ring, and the disc inside keeps a hit area of at least 44px.

tick.why: Each detent tick is printing on the case, flat with no shadow, spaced evenly over the 270 degree sweep.

knob.why: The knob is a raised disc of the same plastic, with a rim drawn as a real border so its edge holds.

primary.why: The unit's one primary knob is dyed orange with a darker rim that holds 3:1 against the plastic body.

key.why: A secondary dial stays body-coloured plastic with a line.ring edge, so it spends none of the unit's orange.

face.why: Only the printed face turns, so the disc's cast shadow keeps falling down and to the right of the single light.

index.why: One printed ink line runs inward from the rim and points at the current detent on the tick ring.

value.why: The current value is printed under the knob with tabular figures so the digits hold still while it turns.

label.why: The printed label names the knob through aria-labelledby, so the name read aloud is the one on the case.

hover.why: Hover moves the orange one step or darkens a key dial's index ink one step and never lifts the knob.

focus-visible.why: Keyboard focus draws the same dark ring with a gap around the disc that every part in dial shows.

aria-disabled=true.why: A disabled knob loses its height and fades to half, while its rim outline stays readable on the body.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduce motion the face jumps to its detent at once and colour steps change with no fade.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the disc, its index and the ticks are drawn as borders in system colours, so none vanish.

background-color.why: The primary knob's orange shifts one step on hover with a brief fade, the same as the primary key.

border-color.why: A key dial's index ink step on hover fades briefly so it reads as a reply rather than a flash.
